newsitem.title: USA: Race case dismissed against Morgan Stanley.
newsitem.headline: Race case dismissed against Morgan Stanley.

text.p: A federal judge has dismissed a discrimination lawsuit brought by two black employees against Morgan Stanley & Co. over electronic mail containing racist jokes.
U.S. District Judge Denise Cote, in a ruling dated Thursday, threw out the suit because it did not state any facts to support the types of discrimination alleged.
However, she ruled that the plaintiffs may file an amended complaint by July 31.
The suit was filed in Manhattan federal court last December by two Morgan Stanley analysts over the offensive e-mail that was circulated among white employees on Oct. 4, 1995.
Among the plaintiffs allegations were that Morgan Stanley intentionally discriminated against them and that the e-mail created a hostile work environment.
Cote said that the only allegation of a hostile work environment in the complaint is the e-mail. She said that a single incident "while entirely reprehensible" cannot form the basis for such a claim.
She also dismissed the plaintiffs' claim of intentional discrimination because the complaint does not state a particular adverse employment decision taken against them. MS.N
